title: Webster's Blue-Backed Speller
sourceTitle: The Elementary Spelling Book: Being an Improvement on the American Spelling Book (revised edition)
author: Noah Webster
licenseEvidence: Internet Archive scan elementaryspelli00web (American Book Company printing, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill copy, full public view). Its copyright page lists entries of 1837, 1857, 1866 and 'Copyright, 1880, by George and Charles Merriam'; the Elementary Spelling Book first appeared in 1829. Published before 1930, so public domain in the USA. Not on Project Gutenberg.
description: Noah Webster's famous "Blue-Backed Speller," the book that taught generations of American children to read and spell. It climbs from two-letter syllables like ba and ab up to six-syllable words, with short reading sentences and seven fables along the way. Each day you review a sound, read a table aloud, spell words from dictation, and copy a sentence. The full scanned book is free online.
includes: 136 lessons in 17 units, covering all 152 numbered tables
The sound key, alphabet, seven fables, and the reference tables on sound-alike words, plurals, numbers, and punctuation
Spelling and phonics questions with answers
A link to the exact page of the free scanned book for every lesson

lessons.title: Analysis of Sounds: Vowels, Consonants, and Diphthongs
steps: Parent: read pp. 8–10 first; then explain that vowels are open sounds and consonants are closed or stopped sounds
Say the long and short sound of each vowel: a (fame, fat), e (mete, met), i (fine, fin), o (note, not), u (mute, but)
Find the straight line (long) and curve (short) marks over vowels on p. 8
questions: Is the sound of b a vowel or a consonant?
What do we call two vowel sounds joined together, like ou in "out"?
Which mark shows a long vowel: a straight line or a curve?
lessons.notes: These pages are mostly for the parent. Teach only the long/short marks now; the rest will come up table by table.

lessons.title: Analysis of Sounds: The Consonant Letters
steps: Read together what the book says about one consonant a day, starting with B, C, and G
Hunt for silent letters: say dumb, gnaw, knave, wring, and listen for the letter you cannot hear
Sort these by the sound of c: cat, cell, cup, city
questions: Does c sound like k or s in "cell"?
How is "when" said: with the h sound first or the w sound first?

lessons.title: Accent and the Key to Pronunciation
steps: Say a two-syllable word like ba-ker and clap on the syllable you say loudest; that is the accent
Read the Key to the Pronunciation on pp. 13–14 and find one example word for each vowel mark
Make a small card of the key to keep in the book for the year
questions: What mark shows the accented syllable in this book?
Does the o in "son" sound like short o or short u?

lessons.title: The Alphabet: Roman, Italic, Old English, and Script
steps: Say the names of the letters from the table on p. 15, pointing to each capital and small letter
Compare the Roman and italic forms of a, g, and k
Copy the small script letters a through g on p. 16
questions: How many letters are in the English alphabet?
What does the character & stand for?
What is the name of the letter h?

lessons.title: Nos. 1–2: ba, be, bi, bo, bu
steps: Read each row of two-letter syllables aloud: ba be bi bo bu, ca ce ci co cu
Read the tiny sentences in No. 1, like "go on" and "is he?"
Write five syllables from the table on a slate or paper
questions: Spell the syllable that sounds like the word "be."
Does ce in No. 1 sound like "see" or "key"?

lessons.title: Nos. 3–4: pa, ra, sa and ab, eb, ib
steps: Read pa pe pi po pu py and ra re ri ro ru ry across the rows
Now read the reversed syllables in No. 4: ab eb ib ob ub, ad ed id od ud
Read the sentence "I am to go in" and copy it
questions: Spell the syllable that starts with r and ends with o.
Which is the reversed form of "ba"?

lessons.title: Nos. 5–7: aj, ak, al and ok, ul, op
steps: Read Nos. 5–7 down the columns: ak ek ik, al el il, am em im
Read the short sentences in No. 6, such as "he is to go up by it"
Copy one sentence from No. 6 with a capital letter at the start
questions: Spell the word made of u and p.
Spell the little word made of o and n.
Read and spell the word in "he is to go up by it" that starts with b.

lessons.title: Nos. 8–9: bra, cra, dra and pra, tra, wra
steps: Blend the two consonants first, then add the vowel: b-r-a, bra
Read the first little sentences in No. 9, like "She fed the old hen"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the syllable made of t, r, and y.
Who did she feed in the sentence from No. 9?

lessons.title: Nos. 10–11: pha, qua, spa and spla, spra
steps: Review: ph sounds like f, and qu sounds like kw
Read the three-letter blends spla, sple, spli, then spra, spre, spri
Write pha, qua, spa, and spra and read them back
questions: What sound does ph make in "pha"?
How many consonants come before the vowel in "spla"?

units.title: Unit 3: Words of Three and Four Letters (Nos. 12–25)

lessons.title: No. 12: cab, lad, bid, rod
steps: Read each column of short words aloud, then read "A new cap" and the little sentences
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
Copy "He has got a new tub."
questions: Spell the word for a boy that rhymes with "bad."
What did he get, in the first sentence?
Spell the opposite of "good" from the table.

lessons.title: No. 13: log, dog, bag, pig
steps: Read the columns: log dog bog, bag rag wag, pig fig wig, jug mug hug
Read the sentences and point to each word from the table
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word that rhymes with "pig" and is a fruit.
Which animal has been fed in the sentences?
Spell the farm animal in the table that rhymes with "wig."

lessons.title: Nos. 14–15: hem, fan, pen; fun, map, top
steps: Read Nos. 14 and 15 aloud, listening for the short vowel in the middle of each word
Sort five words by their middle vowel: a, e, i, o, u
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word that rhymes with "top" and is used to clean floors.
What vowel is in the middle of "pen"?
Spell the word that rhymes with "sun" and means a good time.

lessons.title: No. 16: bat, met, fox, fix
steps: Read the words ending in t and x
Read the sentences, such as "I met six men to-day"
Copy two sentences and underline the words from the table
questions: How many men did I meet?
Spell the animal in No. 16 that ends with x.
What does she have that is new in the first sentence?

lessons.title: Nos. 17–18: babe, cage, lake; bake, mile, yoke
steps: Teach the rule: a final e makes the vowel before it say its name (lak → lake)
Read the long-vowel words in Nos. 17 and 18
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Is the a in "lake" long or short?
Spell the word: a body of water, rhymes with "cake."
Which letter in "bake" makes no sound?

lessons.title: Nos. 19–20: rule, ripe, hope; nine, bone, pure
steps: Review the silent-e rule with u and o: rule, mope, hope, bone
Read every column in Nos. 19 and 20 aloud
Write pairs that change with a final e: rip/ripe, hop/hope, not/note
questions: Add e to "hop." What word do you get?
Is the i in "ripe" long or short?

lessons.title: Nos. 21–22: camp, lamp, scalp; romp, sharp, act
steps: Read the words that end with two consonants: mp, lp, sp, ct
Clap each word: they are all one syllable
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word for a light that rhymes with "camp."

lessons.title: Nos. 23–24: shaft, left, colt; went, wept, last
steps: Read the words ending in ft, lt, nt, pt, and st
Make a list of three words from No. 24 that end in st
Spell 6 words from dictation
questions: Spell the word for a young horse.
Spell the past of "weep" from No. 24.
Which word means the opposite of "first"?

lessons.title: No. 25: fast, best, mist, first
steps: Read the st words: fast, best, rest, west, first, thirst
Read the sentences on p. 25 aloud, such as "Coal and wood will make a fire"
Copy two sentences carefully, with capitals and periods
questions: What will fire burn, according to the first sentence?
Spell the direction where the sun sets.
How long does it take the world to turn round?

lessons.title: No. 26: baker, lady, pony (Two Syllables, Accent on the First)
steps: Read each word in parts, then whole: ba-ker, la-dy, po-ny
Clap the syllables and stress the first one
Read the sentences, such as "A pony is a very little horse," and copy one
questions: What is a pony, says the book?

lessons.title: Nos. 27–28: scab, crib, grub; clam, trim, swim
steps: Read words that begin with two consonants: sc, cr, gr, cl, tr, sw
Make new words by changing the first blend: trim → grim, slim
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the bed for a baby.
Spell the word that rhymes with "trim" and means to move in water.

lessons.title: No. 29: snap, flip, chop, shop
steps: Review the sounds of ch and sh
Read the columns of No. 29 and the sentences below them
Spell 6 words from dictation and copy one sentence
questions: Spell the place where things are sold, rhymes with "chop."
What two letters make the sound at the start of "chop"?

lessons.title: Nos. 30–31: bold, gold, hand; bird, herd, latch
steps: Read the words ending in ld, nd, rd, and tch
Read "A bird sits on a branch to sing" and copy it
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Where does the bird sit to sing?
Spell the metal that rhymes with "bold."
What does "to filch" mean, from No. 31?

lessons.title: No. 32: abase, reclaim, away (Accent on the Second)
steps: Read each word with the stress on the second part: a-way', re-claim'
Compare with No. 26, where the first part was stressed
Read three sentences from p. 29 and copy one
questions: What do men fill balloons with, says the book?
What do teachers like to see their pupils be?

lessons.title: Nos. 33–34: deed, seed, bee; steer, steel, keen
steps: Read all the ee words; ee says long e
Find three ee words that rhyme with "feed"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word that rhymes with "see" and makes honey.
What two letters say long e in these tables?
Spell the strong metal word in No. 34 that rhymes with "feel."

lessons.title: No. 35: coo, loop, boot, troop
steps: Read the oo words: coo, loop, boot, troop, stoop
Read the sentences, such as "Eels swim in the brook"
Copy two sentences and circle every oo
questions: What are sharp tools made of?
What does a man cut trees down with?

lessons.title: Nos. 36–37: back, quick, brick; rock, luck, tank
steps: Read the ck words in No. 36 and the nk and lk words in No. 37
Explain that ck comes right after a short vowel
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word for a baby hen.
Spell the word that rhymes with "duck" and means good fortune.

lessons.title: Nos. 38–39: shrink, mark, ask; snarl, barn, corn
steps: Read the nk, rk, and sk words, then the rl, rn, and rm words
Read "I can play when my task is done" and copy it
Spell 6 words from dictation
questions: Spell where a farmer keeps his hay and animals.
Spell the grain that rhymes with "born."

lessons.title: Nos. 40–42: staff, call, well; push, brass, cross
steps: Read the words ending in double letters: ff, ll, ss
Tell the rule: after a short vowel at the end of a short word, f, l, and s are often doubled
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word that rhymes with "moss" and means angry.

lessons.title: No. 43: egg, eggs; cliff, cliffs (Singular and Plural)
steps: Read the pairs across: one egg, two eggs; one bell, two bells
Read the sentences, such as "A cliff is a high steep rock"
Write the plural of five words from the table
answers: A small lake among the mountains

lessons.title: No. 44, Part 1: banquet, pitcher, candy
steps: Read the first columns in syllables: ban-quet, pitch-er, can-dy
Stress the first syllable of each word
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: No. 44, Part 2: The Reading Sentences
steps: Finish the columns of No. 44
Read the sentences, such as "Silver spoons are not apt to rust"
Copy two sentences from memory, then check
questions: What is cotton velvet like to the touch?
What are not apt to rust?
What should visitors not make too long?

lessons.title: Nos. 45–46: judge, hinge, fringe; bench, catch
steps: Read the dge and nge words, then the ch and tch words
Read the sentences, such as "Doors are hung on hinges"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What does a farmer split rails with?
How long is the first joint of a man's thumb?

lessons.title: Nos. 47–48: rise, nose, guide; spoil, point, loud
steps: Notice that s in rise, wise, and nose sounds like z
Read the oi and ou words in No. 48: spoil, point, coin, loud, round
Read and copy "A sphere is a round body or globe"
questions: Does the s in "nose" sound like s or z?
Spell the word that rhymes with "join" and is money.

lessons.title: No. 49: poach, owl, brown, flour
steps: Read the ow and ou words: owl, cowl, brown, gown, flour, sour
Read the sentences, such as "The owl has large eyes and can see in the night"
Copy two sentences and spell 6 words from dictation
questions: Where do the cat and mouse live?
Spell the color word that rhymes with "town."

units.title: Unit 6: Vowel Pairs and Longer Words (Nos. 50–59)

lessons.title: Nos. 50–51: sea, bead, maid; loaf, chief, teach
steps: Read ea, ai, oa, and ie words; most say the long sound of the first vowel
Read "Few men can afford to keep a coach"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word for the ocean that sounds like the letter c.
What two letters make the long e in "chief"?

lessons.title: Nos. 52–53: break, oak, nail; dream, grain, moan
steps: Read the columns in Nos. 52–53; notice "break" and "steak" sound like long a
Read the sentences, such as "We have green peas in the month of June"
Copy two sentences
questions: In what month do we have green peas?
Which tree grows acorns: oak or pine?
What must girls and boys learn to do?

lessons.title: No. 54: botany, colony, harmony (Three Syllables)
steps: Read each word in three parts: bot-a-ny, col-o-ny
These words are left unmarked: say where the accent falls (always the first syllable here)
Read the definitions, like "Botany is the science of plants"

lessons.title: No. 55: globe, bribe, place, slice
steps: Read the long-vowel words with a silent e: globe, tribe, grace, slice
Read "A glade is an opening among trees" and the other sentences
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the round model of the earth.
Does the c in "place" sound like k or s?

lessons.title: No. 56: banter, letter, doctor, dinner
steps: Read the er and or words, stressing the first syllable
Read the sentences, such as "Never pester the little boys"
Spell 6 words and copy one sentence
questions: When do we have snow and ice?
What do hatters make hats of?

lessons.title: Nos. 57–58: heap, year, spear; near, air, wait
steps: Read the ea, ai, and oa words in Nos. 57–58
Find three words that rhyme with "near"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word that rhymes with "fear" and means 12 months.

lessons.title: No. 59: float, saint, dew, crew
steps: Read the oa, ai, and ew words
Read the sentences, such as "A dog can leap over a fence"
Copy two sentences and spell 6 words from dictation
questions: What can a dog leap over?
Spell the drops on grass in the morning that rhyme with "new."
What kind of rose do we like to see?

units.title: Unit 7: Broad a and Three Syllables (Nos. 60–68)

lessons.title: Nos. 60–61: fraud, awl, dawn; brine, shave, drive
steps: Read the broad a words (au, aw, wa): fraud, yawn, wash, dwarf
Read the long-vowel words in No. 61 and the sentences
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What do we keep salt meat in?
Spell the early morning word that rhymes with "lawn."

lessons.title: Nos. 62–63: dignity, vanity; amazement, excitement
steps: Read No. 62 with stress on the first syllable: van'-i-ty
Read No. 63 with stress on the second: a-maze'-ment
Spell 6 words, saying the syllables as you write
questions: What ending do amazement and excitement share?

lessons.title: Nos. 64–65: selfish, varnish; horseback, padlock
steps: Read the -ish words in No. 64 and the compound words in No. 65
Read the sentences, such as "Riding on horseback is good exercise"
Split three compound words into their two small words
questions: What is good exercise, says the book?
answers: No; he labored for the good of his country

lessons.title: No. 66: senate, private, pirate (Words in -ate)
steps: Read the -ate words; the a here is not a full long a
Read the columns aloud, then the sentences
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What ending do senate and pirate share?

lessons.title: No. 67: luminary, delicacy (Four Syllables)
steps: Read the four-syllable words slowly: lu-mi-na-ry, del-i-ca-cy
Read the sentences about the sun, the moon, and culinary roots
Copy one sentence and mark its four-syllable word
questions: Name a culinary root from the sentences.

lessons.title: No. 68: immortal, maternal, December
steps: Read the three-syllable words with the accent on the second: im-mor'-tal
Say the month names in the table: September, October, November, December
Read and copy "The soul is immortal; it will never die"
questions: Name two utensils from the sentences.

lessons.title: Nos. 69–72: play, boy, claw, salt, shirt
steps: Read the ay, oy, and aw words, then the words where a sounds like o (swamp, wasp)
Read the sentences, such as "The farmer cuts his grass to make hay"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Spell the word that rhymes with "toy."

lessons.title: No. 73: ladder, udder, gander
steps: Read the double-letter words: lad-der, blad-der, rud-der
Read the sentences, such as "Four quarts make a gallon"
Spell 6 words and copy one sentence
questions: How many quarts make a gallon?
What do little boys and girls love to ride in?

lessons.title: No. 74: bracelet, poet, labor, major
steps: Read the words with a long vowel in the first syllable: bra'-ce-let, po'-et, la'-bor
Read the sentences, such as "Men in old age love a quiet life"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Who was a good poet who wrote good songs?
What do ladies wear on their arms?

lessons.title: No. 75: arrival, approval, renewal
steps: Read the -al words with the accent on the second syllable
Read the sentences, such as "We often wait for the arrival of the mail"
Spell 6 words
questions: What do we often wait for the arrival of?

lessons.title: No. 76: overlook, disapprove, intervene
steps: Read the three-syllable words accented on the last part: o-ver-look'
Find small words hidden inside: over, look, approve
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: No. 77: atlas, copy, hurry, poppy
steps: Read the two-syllable words: at-las, cop-y, hur-ry, pop-py
Read the sentences, such as "We cross the ferry in a boat"
Copy two sentences
questions: How do we cross the ferry?
Is the cherry a sweet or an acid fruit, says the book?

lessons.title: No. 78: banishment, tendency, interest
steps: Read three-syllable words accented on the first: ban'-ish-ment
Find the -ment and -cy endings
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: No. 79: aerial, memorial, material
steps: Read four-syllable words with the accent on the second: me-mo'-ri-al
Read the sentences, such as "All clouds float in the aerial regions"
Copy one sentence
questions: Why are gravestones placed by graves?

units.title: Unit 9: More Two- and Three-Syllable Words (Nos. 80–89)

lessons.title: No. 80: muslin, linen, chicken, kitchen
steps: Read the -in, -en, and -ct words: mus-lin, chick-en, sub-ject
Read the sentences, such as "Satin is a rich glossy silk"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What language did the old Romans write in?
Spell the room where food is cooked.

lessons.title: No. 81: inventive, forgetful, successful
steps: Read the -ive and -ful words accented on the second syllable
The last column is left unmarked: say each word and decide where the accent goes
Read and copy "Washington was a successful general"
questions: What ending do forgetful and eventful share?

lessons.title: Nos. 82–83: missionary; relative, marvelous
steps: Read the four-syllable words in No. 82, then the -ive and -ous words in No. 83
Sort five words by ending: -ive or -ous
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: No. 84: bonfire, empire, umpire, brimstone
steps: Read the two-syllable words accented on the first part
Read the sentences, such as "Children should answer questions politely"
Spell 6 words and copy one sentence
answers: It is dug from the earth

lessons.title: No. 85: heroism, porcupine, origin
steps: Read the three-syllable words: her-o-ism, por-cu-pine, or-i-gin
Read the sentences about the porcupine and heroism
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: From whom do all mankind have their origin, says the book?

lessons.title: No. 86: compel, forget, regret, elect
steps: Read the two-syllable words accented on the second part: com-pel', for-get'
Read the sentences, such as "We elect men to make our laws for us"
Copy two sentences
answers: To make our laws for us

lessons.title: No. 87: formal, charcoal, quarrel, squirrel
steps: Read the -al and -el words accented on the first syllable
Read the sentences, such as "Never quarrel with your playmates"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Who climbs a tree quicker: a squirrel or a boy?
What should you never do with your playmates?
answers: Wood charred, or burned to a coal

lessons.title: Nos. 88–89: beaver, weaver, mayor; address, distress
steps: Read No. 88 (accent first) and No. 89 (accent second): ad-dress', dis-tress'
Read the sentences, such as "The weaver weaves yarn into cloth"
Spell 6 words
questions: What will you not do unless you study?

units.title: Unit 10: Longer Words and the th Sound (Nos. 90–99)

lessons.title: No. 90: perennial, terrestrial, evaporate
steps: Read the four-syllable words in parts: per-en'-ni-al
Read the sentences, such as "The sun will evaporate water on the ground"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What will the sun do to water on the ground?
How long does a triennial assembly last?

lessons.title: No. 91: acquire, admire, adore, before
steps: Read the -ire and -ore words with the accent on the second syllable
Read the sentences, such as "People admire the beautiful flowers of spring"
Copy two sentences
questions: What do people admire in spring?
What does a field require to secure the crops?

lessons.title: No. 92: between, ordain, complain, explain
steps: Read the -ain and -een words accented on the last syllable
Read the sentences about the moon, the earth, and astronomy
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What passes between the earth and the sun in an eclipse of the sun?
What science explains the causes of day and night?

lessons.title: Nos. 93–94: entertainment, desperado; cinnamon, skeleton
steps: Read No. 93 (full accent on the third syllable), then No. 94 (left unmarked for practice)
Read the sentences about "engage" and "preengage"
Spell 6 words

lessons.title: No. 95: numerous, humorous, treacherous
steps: Read the -ous words: nu-mer-ous, hu-mor-ous, treach-er-ous
Make a list of five -ous words
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What ending do these words share?

lessons.title: No. 96: theme, three, north, truth
steps: Practice the breathy th (thin, three) and the voiced th (this, then)
Read the th words in No. 96 and the sentences
Copy "A manly youth will speak the truth"
questions: What does a manly youth speak?

lessons.title: No. 97: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, filbert
steps: Read the days of the week in the table and spell each one
Read the other two-syllable words accented on the first
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Which letter in "Wednesday" is not sounded?

lessons.title: No. 98: borrow, elbow, shadow, narrow
steps: Read the -ow words; the ow has its long o sound here
Read the sentences, such as "A ship or boat must have ballast"
Spell 6 words and copy one sentence
questions: What sound does ow have in "shadow"?
Why must a ship have ballast?
Spell the joint in the middle of your arm.

lessons.title: No. 99: treatise, oatmeal, floral, plural
steps: Read the two-syllable words accented on the first part
Read the sentences, such as "An egg is nearly oval in shape"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
answers: The post round which winding stairs are formed

lessons.title: No. 100: anonymous, amphibious, miraculous
steps: Read the four-syllable -ous words: a-non'-y-mous
Read the sentences explaining each hard word
Copy one sentence
questions: What does an anonymous author not do?
What can an amphibious animal do?
answers: Live in different elements (on land and in water)

lessons.title: No. 101: majority, dexterity, humility
steps: Read the -ity words; this table is left unmarked, so say the accent yourself
Read the sentences, such as "A majority is more than half"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: Nos. 102–103: imaginary; compatibility
steps: Read the five-syllable words of No. 102, then the six-syllable words of No. 103
Clap every syllable of "compatibility"
Read and copy "Epistolary correspondence is carried on by letters"
questions: How is epistolary correspondence carried on?
Who were cotemporary authors, says the book?

lessons.title: No. 104: benefit, alphabet, elephant
steps: Read the three-syllable words accented on the first: ben'-e-fit, al'-pha-bet
Find the -ant words: elephant, elegant, ignorant
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What sound does ph make in "alphabet"?

lessons.title: No. 105: opportunity, punctuality
steps: Read the five-syllable words accented on the third: op-por-tu'-ni-ty
Say each word slowly, then fast
Spell 4–6 words, one syllable at a time

lessons.title: No. 106, Part 1: plantation, vacation, quotation
steps: Learn that -tion says "shun"
Read the first half of the -tion words
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: No. 106, Part 2: temptation, location, and more
steps: Finish the -tion words of No. 106
Make a list of five -tion words you use at home
Spell 6 words
questions: What word in -tion means a place?

lessons.title: No. 107: publication, navigation, legislation
steps: Read the four-syllable -tion words accented on the third
Read the sentences about legislators
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Who chooses legislators in free governments?

lessons.title: No. 108: definite, opposite, appetite, anecdote
steps: Read the -ite and -ote words accented on the first
Read and copy "An anecdote is a short story"
Spell 6 words

lessons.title: No. 109: condense, resolve, embark
steps: Read the two-syllable words accented on the second
Read the sentences, such as the one about the brave sailors
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What do the brave sailors do?
Who outlived all the people who lived before them?
answers: Embark on board of ships and sail away

lessons.title: No. 110: agreement, engagement, opponent
steps: Read the three-syllable -ment and -ent words accented on the second
Read the sentences explaining "remainder" and "retirement"
Spell 6 words
answers: That which remains or is left

lessons.title: No. 111: estimate, celebrate, separate
steps: Read the -ate words accented on the first syllable
Read the sentences, such as the one about emulating good people
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
answers: One who defends the cause of another
Those of great and good men

lessons.title: No. 112: villain, curtain, dolphin, mittens
steps: Read the words where ai or i is unclear: cur-tain, vil-lain
Read the sentences, such as "A curtain is used to hide something from the view"
Copy two sentences
questions: What is a curtain used for?
Spell the sea animal with beautiful colors.

lessons.title: No. 113: sentinel, furniture, handkerchief
steps: Read the three-syllable words accented on the first
Notice the note on how "handkerchief" is said
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
answers: A fortress to defend a city or town
A supplement or addition to a will

lessons.title: Nos. 114–115: author, saucy, tawny; captive, stocking
steps: Read the au and aw words in No. 114 (a as in all)
Read No. 115 and its sentences
Spell 6 words
questions: What color is the skin of the Indian, says the book?
How many cents equal one quarter of a dollar?
What kind of fowl is the peacock?
answers: A gaudy, vain, and noisy fowl

lessons.title: No. 116: motion, nation, lotion, mansion
steps: Read the two-syllable -tion and -sion words
Read the sentences, such as "A mansion is a place of residence"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
answers: A daily allowance for a soldier
A place of residence, or dwelling

lessons.title: No. 117: democracy, geography, biography
steps: Read the four-syllable words accented on the second
Read the sentences explaining each "-graphy" word
Copy two definitions
answers: A history of a person's life

lessons.title: No. 118: diagonal, millennium, republican
steps: Read the four-syllable words accented on the second
Clap and spell "di-ag-o-nal"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: Nos. 119–120: congratulate; librarian, victorious
steps: Read the -ate words of No. 119 and the -ian and -ious words of No. 120
Read the sentences, such as "A library is a collection of books"
Spell 6 words
questions: Which insect is a pattern of industry?
answers: A person who has charge of a library

lessons.title: No. 121: individuality, incompressibility
steps: Read the seven- and eight-syllable words very slowly
Count the syllables of "in-di-vid-u-al-i-ty" on your fingers
Pick one long word and spell it syllable by syllable
lessons.notes: A fun challenge table for older children; younger ones can just clap the syllables.

lessons.title: Nos. 122–123: thirteen, theory; mother, weather
steps: No. 122 has the breathy th (thir-teen); No. 123 has the voiced th (moth-er)
Read both tables, feeling the throat buzz on the voiced th
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Is the th in "mother" voiced or breathy?
Is the th in "thirteen" voiced or breathy?
Who are the heathen, says the book?

lessons.title: No. 124: accomplish, establish, astonish
steps: Read the -ish words accented on the second syllable
Read the sentences, such as "Laws are abolished by the same power that made them"
Spell 6 words
questions: Who can accomplish a great deal?
What do wars generally prove to all parties?
answers: A man who saves the fragments of time

lessons.title: No. 125: ceremonial, testimonial, equatorial
steps: Read the five-syllable words accented on the third
Read the sentences, such as "old men for counsel, young men for war"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Which animal is the link between quadrupeds and fowls?
answers: Acts that happen at the same time

lessons.title: No. 126: twelve, shelf, fresh; this, path, paths
steps: Read the one-syllable words in the first columns
Read the voiced th words (the, this, them) and the plurals path/paths, mouth/mouths
Copy "Great haste often makes waste"
questions: How many things make a dozen?
What does great haste often make?

lessons.title: No. 127: whale, wheat, which; who, whole
steps: Say wh words with a puff of breath first: whale (hwale), when (hwen)
Then read the words where w is silent: who, whom, whose, whole
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What are the largest of marine animals?
answers: The thin watery part of milk

lessons.title: No. 128: exact, exist, example (x like gz)
steps: Read the words where x sounds like gz: ex-act' (eg-zact)
Read the sentences, such as "It is useful to keep very exact accounts"
Spell 6 words
questions: What sound does x make in "exact"?
What is it useful to keep, says the book?

lessons.title: Nos. 129–130: question, Christian; alien, savior; glazier, illusion
steps: Read the -tion words said like "chun" (ques-tion), then the words where i sounds like y (al-ien)
Read the -sier, -zier, and -sion words in No. 130 (zh sound)
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What sound does si make in "illusion"?

lessons.title: No. 131: Christ, scheme, ache, chorus, school
steps: Read the words where ch sounds like k
Read the sentences, such as "An epoch is a fixed point of time"
Spell 6 words
questions: What sound does ch make in "school"?
answers: The milky fluid separated from food by digestion

lessons.title: Nos. 132–133: gift, tiger, dagger; tragic, agile, legible
steps: No. 132: g is hard (as in go) even before e, i, y: gear, gift, girl
No. 133: c and g ending an accented syllable are soft: trag-ic, ag-ile, leg-i-ble
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Is the g in "gift" hard or soft?
Is the g in "agile" hard or soft?

units.title: Unit 14: Silent Letters and Word Endings (Nos. 134–146)

lessons.title: Nos. 134–135: conscious, partial; precious, ambition
steps: ci, ti, and si can say "sh": con-scious, par-tial, pre-cious
Read both tables aloud
Spell 6 words
questions: What sound does ti make in "partial"?

lessons.title: Nos. 136–137, Part 1: associate, appreciate; critic, logic
steps: Read No. 136: ci and ti say "shi" (as-so-shi-ate)
Begin No. 137: words in -ic and -ical, such as critic, critical
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: No. 137, Part 2: Words in -ical and -istic
steps: Finish the columns of No. 137
Read the sentences, such as the one about thermometrical observations
Spell 6 words
questions: What ending turns "critic" into a word that describes?

lessons.title: Nos. 138–139: civilize, organize; characterize
steps: Read the -ize words: au-thor-ize, civ-il-ize, or-gan-ize
Find the root word in each: author, civil, organ
Read the sentence about tyrannizing over the weak and copy it
questions: What is the root word in "realize"?
Over whom should we never tyrannize?
What ending do these words share?

lessons.title: No. 140: song, string; finger, anger
steps: Read the ng words with the plain sound: sing, song, bring
Then read the words where ng is followed by a hard g: fin-ger, an-ger, hun-ger
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: In "finger," do you hear a hard g after the ng?
In "singer," do you hear a hard g?

lessons.title: No. 141: capture, culture, feature
steps: Read the -ture words: cap-ture, cul-ture, fea-ture
Read the sentences, such as the one about the lungs
Spell 6 words
questions: What are the lungs the organs of?

lessons.title: Nos. 142–143: gnat, knack, knead; machine, magazine
steps: Read the words where g and k before n are silent
Then read the words where ch says sh (machine, chaise)
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: What sound does ch make in "machine"?
What should you do to the dough to have good bread?

lessons.title: Nos. 144–146: bread, health; sign, assign; bacon, bitten
steps: No. 144: ea says short e (bread, dead, health)
No. 145: g is silent in sign and assign, but heard in signify
No. 146: the vowel before n is silent in bacon and bitten
questions: What vowel sound does ea make in "bread"?

lessons.title: The Dog, The Stag, and The Squirrel
steps: Read the three short animal pieces aloud, taking turns
Tell back one of them in your own words
Copy two hard words and their meaning: mastiff, pricket
questions: What kind of dog is the mastiff used as?
What is the female of the red deer called?
Where do gray squirrels make their nests?
answers: On the high branches of trees

lessons.title: Fable I: Of the Boy That Stole Apples
steps: Read the fable together
Tell it back: the boy, the old man, the grass, the stones
Copy the moral in your own words
questions: What did the old man first throw at the boy?
What finally made the boy come down?
What is the lesson of the fable?
answers: If kind words fail, the wicked must be dealt with more severely

lessons.title: Fable II: The Country Maid and Her Milk Pail
steps: Read the fable aloud
List the maid's dreams in order: eggs, chickens, a new gown
Tell what went wrong and why
questions: What was the maid carrying on her head?
What color gown did she want?
answers: It fell and spilled when she tossed her head

lessons.title: Fable III: The Two Dogs
steps: Read the fable aloud
Tell it back, naming Tray and Tiger
Talk about choosing friends wisely
questions: Which dog was the good-natured spaniel?
What did Tiger do in the village?
answers: Because he was found in bad company

lessons.title: Fable IV: The Partial Judge
steps: Read the fable aloud
Act out the farmer and the lawyer
Discuss what "partial" means here
questions: Whose bull gored the ox at first, in the farmer's story?
How did the lawyer change when he learned it was his own bull?
answers: He wanted to look into the case instead of paying
Be as ready to do justice to others as to demand it from them

lessons.title: Fable V: The Cat and the Rat
steps: Read the fable aloud
Tell the cat's two tricks in order
Copy the old rat's saying about caution in your own words
questions: What was the cat's first trick?
Where did she hide the second time?
What did the old rat say caution is the parent of?
answers: Hanging by her feet from a hook, pretending to be dead
In the bottom of a meal tub, covered in flour

lessons.title: Fable VI: The Fox and the Bramble
steps: Read the fable aloud
Tell why the fox stopped complaining about the thorns
Talk about a time something hard also kept you safe
questions: What good did the brambles do?
answers: They kept off the dogs and saved his life

lessons.title: Fable VII: The Bear and the Two Friends
steps: Read the fable aloud
Tell what each friend did when the bear came
Discuss what a true friend does in danger
questions: What did the first friend do?
What did the other friend do?
answers: Lay flat and pretended to be dead
Never to go with a friend who deserts you in danger

lessons.title: Days, Weeks, and Hours
steps: Read the questions and answers about time aloud, one person asking and one answering
Say the days of the week in order and spell two of them
Tell what makes day and night
questions: How many days are in a year?
How many hours in a day and night?

units.title: Unit 16: Words Alike and Not Alike (No. 148)

lessons.title: Words Nearly Alike: accept and except
steps: Read each pair and its meaning: accept / except, affect / effect
Say both words of each pair carefully so they sound different
Write three pairs with their meanings
questions: Which means "to take": accept or except?
Which means "with a great voice": aloud or allowed?

lessons.title: Words Spelled Alike but Said Differently; Sound-Alikes (ail to climb)
steps: Read the words spelled the same but said differently
Begin the sound-alike words: aunt / ant, ark / arc, climb / clime
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Which is a vessel: ark or arc?
Which means "to ascend": climb or clime?

lessons.title: Sound-Alike Words: council to wreak
steps: Read the pairs and their meanings: hale / hail, lesson / lessen
Choose the right word in spoken sentences
Write three pairs with meanings
questions: Which means "to diminish": lesson or lessen?
Which means "to revenge": reek or wreak?

lessons.title: Sound-Alike Words: rest to the end of the list
steps: Finish the list of pairs: vain / vein, vice / vise, weigh / way
Read the first sentences that use the pairs, such as "An oak bears acorns"
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book
questions: Which carries blood: vain or vein?
Which means "to find the weight": weigh or way?

lessons.title: Sound-Alike Sentences, Part 1
steps: Read the sentences aloud and find the sound-alike word in each
Take dictation of three sentences; the child must choose the right spelling
Check against the book
questions: What does the Niagara River pour down?
Which is a large gun: cannon or canon?
Spell the word in "Bears live in the woods" that sounds like "bares."

lessons.title: Sound-Alike Sentences, Part 2
steps: Read the rest of the sentences
Make up your own sentence for two pairs, such as sleigh / slay
Spell 6 words
questions: What does a sleigh run on?

units.title: Unit 17: Spelling Rules and Reference Tables (Nos. 149–152)

lessons.title: No. 149: Words of Irregular Spelling
steps: Read the words that are not said the way they are spelled, with the book's way of saying them
Pick five and practice: one, once, done, gone, half
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: No. 149: Silent Letters
steps: Read the lists of silent letters: l in calf and walk, h after r, g before n
Find the silent letter in each word you read
Spell 6 words

lessons.title: No. 150: Rules for Verbs (-ed and -ing)
steps: Read rules 1–5: add ed and ing; double the last consonant after a single short vowel
Read rules 6–12 about the agent (-er) and verbs ending in e, y, and ie
Write the -ed and -ing forms of hop, play, and carry

lessons.title: Plurals of Nouns
steps: Read rules 13–18 for making plurals
Make plurals: box, lady, day, leaf, church
Check each one by its rule

lessons.title: Making New Words: -y, -ly, -ness, -less, -ful
steps: Read the tables of words made by adding endings
Build words: hand + y, kind + ness, care + less, joy + ful
Write five new words and use one in a sentence

lessons.title: Of Numbers: Figures, Roman Numerals, and Number Words
steps: Read the table of figures, letters (Roman numerals), and names
Write 1–20 in Roman numerals
Spell the ordinal words first through tenth

lessons.title: Words and Phrases from Foreign Languages
steps: Read a handful of the phrases and their English meanings
Pick three you have heard before and say what they mean
Copy one phrase and its meaning
answers: I came, I saw, I conquered
The terms being turned around (the other way round)
lessons.notes: Choose phrases suited to your child's age; this table is mostly for older students.

lessons.title: Abbreviations Explained
steps: Read the list of abbreviations with their meanings
Find abbreviations you see in daily life: Mr., Mrs., No., P.O.
Write five abbreviations and what they stand for

lessons.title: Punctuation and Capital Letters
steps: Read about each mark: comma, semicolon, colon, period, question, exclamation, dash, apostrophe
Read the rules for capital letters
Copy a sentence from the fables and name every mark in it
questions: Does a person's name begin with a capital letter?
answers: That a letter or letters are left out
A sudden stop or change of subject

lessons.title: No. 151: qu Words, Silent t, and ei / ie
steps: Read the qu words (liquid, equity) and the words with silent t (glisten, chasten)
Learn the two ei and ie tables; memorize a few of each
Spell 6–8 words from the columns from dictation, then check them against the book

lessons.title: No. 152, Part 1: Words Difficult to Spell (abeyance to journal)
steps: Read the first groups of hard words with their sayings in parentheses
Choose 6 words suited to your child and practice them
Spell them from dictation

lessons.title: No. 152, Part 2: Words Difficult to Spell (to the end)
steps: Read the rest of the hard words, including the French words at the end
Choose 6 words and practice them
Spell them from dictation, then review any from Part 1 you missed
